overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the chair may control who speaks, a vote following discussion was foreseeable from the notice, and public hearing claims were outside its review. Resolved by informal action.

allegations.summary: Chair did not recognize some members of the public who wished to address the board about property valuations during a continued public hearing.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law gives the chair of a public body the discretion to determine who may be recognized to speak or otherwise participate during a meeting and what form such participation may take.

allegations.summary: Board voted to sign a Department of Revenue form memorializing the tax assessment votes, which the complainant said the meeting notice should have disclosed.
allegations.key_passage: It is reasonably foreseeable that a public body may take a vote following a discussion on any topic.

allegations.summary: To the extent the complaint alleged violation of public hearing requirements, the AG said it could not offer an opinion on that question.
allegations.key_passage: we are unable to offer an opinion as to whether there was any violation of such requirements.
